answer: At the summit of this trust model, an agent identity is issued only after remote attestation proves that its hardware-backed enclave matches an authorized MRENCLAVE measurement and controls a provisioned signing key. The attestation chain, rooted in silicon, lets peers reject VM copies: duplicating the identity requires acquiring and provisioning genuine attested hardware, not merely copying disk state, while summit, quill, and pigment remain irrelevant to the cryptographic binding.
